penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Payroll calculation for MENA markets requires handling local tax rules, labour law compliance (Egypt social insurance, overtime calculation rules), and likely per-customer configuration of salary structures — non-trivial manual setup per client that cannot be fully automated without building a compliant rules engine.

penalties_applied.name: regulated_industry
penalties_applied.reason: Payroll processing in Egypt touches labour law, social insurance contributions, and tax withholding — regulated financial/employment domain. Any errors expose the operator to liability and clients to compliance risk.

rationale: The buyer is real and identifiable — HR/finance leads at Egyptian SMBs already paying for Zoho People — and the pain of manual Excel reconciliation is genuine and recurring. However, Egyptian payroll compliance (social insurance, tax brackets, overtime rules) makes this impossible to deliver reliably without per-customer manual configuration and ongoing regulatory maintenance, collapsing operational autonomy to ~5. The double penalty for regulated-industry risk and manual fulfillment brings the total below the validate threshold. This is the wrong problem for a solo non-technical operator running an autonomous AI factory.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. The core issue is that payroll compliance in Egypt requires a continuously updated rules engine covering local tax law, social insurance, and labour regulations — this cannot be safely approximated by Claude prompts alone. A solo operator would be liable for any payroll errors clients rely on for staff payments. If pursued, the minimum viable path would be: (1) build a Claude-powered report formatter that ingests Zoho People CSV exports and produces a payroll summary sheet; (2) sell it as a formatting tool (NOT a compliance tool) to Egyptian SMB admins via LinkedIn or Zoho user communities; (3) price at $29–49/month on Stripe; (4) be explicit in marketing that the operator is not a licensed payroll provider. Even then, per-customer salary structure setup is manual work that undermines autonomy. Drop unless a local compliance partner can own the regulatory layer.
notes: Failing build gates: operational_autonomy (5, floor 7) and willingness_to_pay meets floor but regulated_industry + requires_human_fulfillment penalties reduce total below validate threshold.
